subject_lessons.title: Y6 Math: Ratios, Percentages, Negative Numbers & [-1, 1] Normalization
subject_lessons.story:
TRADITIONAL MATH LESSON (GRADE 6):
• Ratios & Proportions compare two quantities: if a rocket has 120 fuel out of a 160 capacity, the ratio is `120 / 160 = 0.75` (or `75%`).
• Negative Numbers (`< 0`) represent opposite directions: `-3.5 m/s` means moving left, `+3.5 m/s` means moving right.
• Neural networks work best when inputs are normalized into the ratio `[-1.0, +1.0]`!

# 📐 YEAR 6 MATH ASSIGNMENT: Ratios & Sensor Normalization
raw_x = 170.0
pad_x = 320.0
half_width = 300.0

print(f'Raw x={raw_x} relative to pad={pad_x} -> Normalized Ratio: {normalized_x:.2f}')
assert -1.0 <= normalized_x <= 1.0

subject_lessons.title: Y6 Science: Cell Biology, Biological Neurons & Thermal Energy
subject_lessons.story:
TRADITIONAL SCIENCE LESSON (GRADE 6):
Your brain contains 86 billion biological nerve cells called Neurons!
  1. Dendrites receive incoming signals (Inputs).
  2. The Soma (cell body) sums the signals together.
  3. The Axon fires an electrical pulse across Synapses to the next neuron (Output)!
Artificial Neural Networks in SynapseOS are directly modeled on biological dendrites, somas, and synapses.

# 🔬 YEAR 6 BIOLOGY LAB: Dendrites, Soma & Axon Firing
import math
dendrite_inputs = [0.8, -0.4, 0.5]
synapse_weights = [1.2, 0.5, 0.9]
soma_sum = sum(x * w for x, w in zip(dendrite_inputs, synapse_weights))
axon_output = math.tanh(soma_sum)
print(f'Soma Sum: {soma_sum:.2f} -> Axon Firing Output: {axon_output:.3f}')

TRADITIONAL LANGUAGE ARTS LESSON (GRADE 6):
• An Unsupported Opinion is a feeling without data ("I think my AI is really smart").
• A Verifiable Claim cites specific measurements ("Increasing hidden neurons from 2 to 10 raised classification accuracy from 68% to 94%").

subject_lessons.story:
TRADITIONAL ANCIENT HISTORY LESSON (GRADE 6):
• Mesopotamia invented cuneiform writing and base-60 math (60 seconds in a minute, 360° in a circle!).
• Ancient Egypt used geometry to survey the Nile River.
• Ancient Greece (Socrates, Plato, Aristotle, Euclid) developed formal logic and the Socratic Method—teaching by asking guiding questions, just like Lumi!

# 🤖 YEAR 6 AI CAPSTONE: Normalizing Sensor Ratios for a Neural Brain
from workbench.labs.neat_core import NEATPopulation

pop = NEATPopulation(num_inputs=4, num_outputs=2, pop_size=20)
obs = [(280.0 - 320.0) / 300.0, (365.0 - 120.0) / 350.0, -1.2 / 6.0, 0.8 / 6.0]
out = pop.best_genome.forward(obs)
print('Normalized Inputs:', [round(x, 3) for x in obs], '-> Outputs:', [round(y, 3) for y in out])
